Polywrap Films is our only qualified supplier of the 23-micron stretch film used on all four pallet wrappers. Qualifying a new supplier takes about four months (trials plus customer sign-off). We use roughly 9 tonnes a month.

state: Incident note, Saturday 24 Oct, 11:30. Brightloom's autumn code FALL15 was meant to give 15% off orders over £60 on full-price home textiles. It went live at 08:00 on the site banner and in an email to 48,000 subscribers. A setup error left out the £60 minimum and let the code stack with the existing 20% clearance discount, so clearance items are going out at 35% off. Since 08:00, 1,140 orders have used FALL15; a normal Saturday morning brings about 400 orders in total. A deal-forum thread titled "Brightloom stacking glitch", posted at 09:50, has 600 replies. On clearance items at 35% off our margin is about -4%; on full-price items at 15% off it is about +28%. 62% of FALL15 orders contain clearance items. Customer Peter Lund, 58, made two transfers from his current account to an account named 'J. Morgan Logistics': 1,500 on 24 November and 3,200 on 26 November. state: Incident prep note, 22 Nov 2027, 09:30. On 20 Nov at 16:05 an outside researcher emailed security@ to report that our document app's public share links (/s/{token}) still return a file when the last 4 characters of the token are removed, because the lookup uses a prefix match. The researcher attached two sample links that opened other customers' files: a payroll spreadsheet with staff names and salaries, and a signed contract. The email sat unread in the shared inbox over the weekend; the on-call engineer read it at 09:12 today and reproduced the flaw by 09:25. Code history shows the prefix match shipped in release 3.14 on 2 Oct. Access logs since 2 Oct show 1,840 successful requests using shortened tokens, from 23 distinct IP addresses, 2 of which belong to the researcher. A patch that requires an exact token match is written and tested; deploying it takes 15 minutes. Security policy: confirmed exposure of customer personal data is reported to the privacy officer within 24 hours of confirmation, and affected customers are told within 72 hours of confirmation.

q1.instructions: The researcher's report included examples of exposed files.

criteria.true: Sample links to other customers' files were attached.
criteria.false: The report described the flaw without examples.

q2.instructions: The logs suggest that people other than the researcher used the flaw.

criteria.true: Shortened-token requests came from addresses not linked to the researcher.
criteria.false: All such requests came from the researcher.

q3.instructions: Judged by what stops further exposure soonest, what should the on-call engineer do first?

criteria.Reply to researcher: Thank the researcher and agree disclosure terms.

q4.instructions: How severe is this incident?
criteria: Informational: No real weakness.
Low: A weakness with no realistic path to customer data.
Medium: Customer data could be reached, but no sign it has been.
High: Customer data reached by a known party, flaw now closed.
Critical: Customer personal data reached by unknown parties while the flaw is still open.

q5.instructions: Which customers should be treated as affected and told?

criteria.Two sample owners: Only the owners of the two files in the report.
criteria.All customers: Every customer of the document app.
criteria.No one yet: Nobody until a full external audit is complete.
criteria.Owners of accessed files: Owners of every file fetched with a shortened token since 2 Oct.

state: Duty scientist's note, 07:30, 18 July 2027. Routine overnight samples from Hillcrest service reservoir: total coliforms detected in 2 of 3 samples (target: none detected); E. coli not detected in any sample; chlorine residual 0.08 mg/L (operating minimum 0.2 mg/L). Hillcrest supplies about 6,400 homes and St Anne's Hospital. Yesterday at 15:00 a roof hatch on the reservoir was found unlatched after storm damage; it was secured at 16:10. Customer contacts since midnight: 3 about taste, none about illness. Water safety procedure: (1) if E. coli is found in any sample, issue a boil-water notice at once. (2) If coliforms are found while chlorine is below the operating minimum: raise chlorine dosing; isolate the reservoir if an alternative supply exists; resample within 6 hours; inform the health authority the same day. A boil-water notice then follows only if resampling finds E. coli or the health authority advises one. The procedure says nothing about contacting individual customers. Westfield reservoir can supply Hillcrest's zone for up to 48 hours.

City rule: removing a tree with a trunk diameter of 30 cm or more, measured 1.4 m above the ground, needs a permit. A permit is granted when (a) a certified arborist reports the tree dead, dying or hazardous; (b) the tree is within 3 m of a building's foundation and is damaging it; or (c) the tree must be removed for construction under an approved building permit. Intake memo, Halden Legal, 3 February 2027.

Prospective client: Renata Diaz, co-founder of Crumb & Co, a bakery. She and her former partner, Luis Moreno, each owned 50%. Luis left in October 2026. Renata says he took a copy of the customer list and opened a competing bakery two streets away; three wholesale customers, about 30% of revenue, have moved to him.

Renata has a copy of their partnership agreement with a clause saying neither partner may compete within 5 km for 12 months after leaving. The copy she has is signed by her only. She believes Luis signed his copy and that it is "probably in a box from the old office", which she has not searched yet. She has emails from two of the wholesale customers saying Luis contacted them in November.

Renata wants the firm to act on a no-win-no-fee basis. Firm policy: no-win-no-fee is offered only when the reviewing partner judges the chance of success at 60% or more AND the likely recovery is at least 3 times the expected costs. Expected costs to trial: about 40,000. Her accountant estimates lost profit at 85,000 a year; the clause, if valid, covers 12 months. Renata could also pay hourly; she has savings of about 15,000, and an early case review costs about 2,500.

Note to the permits officer, 22 October 2027.

Application NE-27-044 from Brennick Civil Ltd asks for a noise exemption to resurface Station Road overnight, 23:00 to 05:00, on 4 nights, 8 to 11 November 2027. City noise rule: construction noise is not allowed from 22:00 to 07:00 in residential areas without an exemption. An exemption may be granted only when (a) daytime work would cause serious traffic disruption or a safety risk, and (b) every address within 100 m receives written notice at least 7 full days before work starts (not counting the day the notice is delivered or the first day of work). The officer may attach conditions to an exemption.

Station Road carries about 22,000 vehicles a day and is the main route to the hospital; the transport department supports night work. Brennick plans to deliver letters to 140 addresses on 2 November. Noise forecast at the nearest homes: 78 dB on nights 1 and 2 (milling), 65 dB on nights 3 and 4 (paving).

The residents' association objects, pointing to 3 earlier overnight jobs on the same road this year, and asks for work to stop by 01:00 each night. A care home is 40 m from the works. Brennick has offered hotel rooms to residents of homes within 30 m during the two milling nights.

Hana runs a shop selling hand-dyed yarn on an online marketplace. The marketplace measures sellers over the last 90 days: the late shipment rate (late orders divided by all orders) must stay below 4%, and the order defect rate (orders with a buyer claim, a one- or two-star review, or a refund, divided by all orders) must stay below 1%. She has missed two appointments without notice, on 14 July and 2 September 2026. Clinic policy: after two missed appointments without notice within 6 months, the patient is discharged to the GP unless the clinician judges that discharge would put the patient at risk; patients aged 75 or over, or with a recorded memory problem, must be phoned before any discharge decision.

On 4 September her daughter rang to say her mother had not received the appointment letters, because they went to her old address; she moved into sheltered housing on 1 July. The address on file is still the old one. The daughter's call was logged by reception but no appointment was discussed. Mrs Pike's next booked appointment is 23 September 2026, and its letter was posted on 1 September to the address on file. The waiting list for new physiotherapy referrals is 11 weeks.

q1.instructions: How many appointments has she missed without notice in the last 6 months?
criteria: None: No missed appointments.
One: One missed appointment.
Two: Two missed appointments.
Three or more: Three or more missed appointments.

q2.instructions: How likely is it that the missed appointments were outside her control?
criteria: Very unlikely: Nothing suggests she could not have attended.
Unlikely: A weak or unsupported explanation.
Possible: A plausible explanation with nothing to back it up.
Likely: A plausible explanation backed by one other fact.
Very likely: An explanation that the clinic's own records confirm.

q3.instructions: How much risk would discharging her to the GP now carry?
criteria: Low: Little harm if treatment is delayed.
Moderate: Some loss of progress, but no added danger.
High: A real chance of another fall or injury while she waits again.

q4.instructions: How likely is it that Mrs Pike knows about her 23 September appointment?
criteria: Unlikely: Nothing suggests the details have reached her.
Uncertain: She may have heard by some route, but it cannot be confirmed.
Likely: She has been told or has received the letter.

q5.instructions: What should the clinic do next?

criteria.Discharge to GP: Apply the two-missed-appointments rule and discharge.
criteria.Phone, update, confirm: Phone her or her daughter, update the address and confirm the 23 September appointment.
criteria.Leave booking as is: Keep the 23 September appointment and take no other action.

Clauses 4.2 to 4.6 apply to all grower deliveries of stone fruit, pome fruit and brassicas received at the Ashby Road site (Gate 2 and Gate 3).

4.6 Records

7. Quotation and tender thresholds

7.1 Requests for goods and services with an estimated total value of £5,000 or less (excluding VAT) may be procured by direct award from a single supplier, provided the budget holder records the award on form PF-14.

7.2 Requests with an estimated total value above £5,000 and below £25,000 (excluding VAT) require at least three written quotations, to be retained on the procurement file.

UNIVERSITY OF WESTBRIDGE – PROCUREMENT SERVICES
Procurement Policy Extract: Low-Value and Small Tenders
Document ref: PS-POL-07, Issue 4 (effective 1 September 2026)

7.1 Scope
7.1.1 This section applies to goods and services procurements with an estimated total contract value of £5,000 or more and below £75,000 (inclusive of VAT), referred to in this policy as "small tenders".
7.1.2 Requisitioners must not split a requirement into separate purchases to avoid the thresholds in 7.1.1.

7.2 Evaluation
7.2.1 Tenders shall be evaluated on a weighted basis of 70% price and 30% quality, unless the Tender Notice states otherwise.
7.2.2 Each evaluation panel shall consist of no fewer than three members, one of whom shall be a budget holder from the requesting department.
7.2.3 The panel chair shall record the moderated quality score for each supplier in the Tender Evaluation Record (form PS-F-19) within five working days of the moderation meeting.

7.3 Pricing and Totals
7.3.1 Where a supplier's submitted total differs from the sum of its line items, the line-item total shall prevail, and the discrepancy shall be recorded on form PS-F-19.
7.3.2 Price scores shall be calculated as: (lowest compliant price ÷ supplier price) × 70.

7.4 Exceptions
7.4.1 The Director of Procurement may approve award to a supplier scoring below the quality threshold where the requirement is time-critical and no compliant alternative is available within the Tender Notice validity period.
7.4.2 Clause 7.4.1 does not apply where the shortfall in quality score exceeds 10 points out of 100.
7.4.3 Any award under 7.4.1 must be reported to the Finance Committee at its next scheduled meeting.

7.5 Conflicts of Interest
7.5.1 Panel members must declare any interest in a bidding supplier before scoring begins. A declaration received after scoring has started shall be referred to the Head of Procurement.

SECTION 7: BILLING ADJUSTMENTS AND ESTIMATED READINGS

7.1 Where a customer's account has been billed on an estimated reading for two or more consecutive billing periods, the billing team must obtain an actual meter reading before the third bill is issued.

7.2 Estimated bills must be calculated using the customer's average daily consumption over the previous 12 months, multiplied by the number of days in the billing period, then adjusted for the seasonal factor in Table 7B.

7.3 Where a meter reading subsequently obtained shows that a previous estimate was incorrect, the difference must be credited or debited to the account in the next available billing cycle. Adjustments above £150.00 require sign-off by a Billing Team Leader.

7.4 Adjustments must be recorded on the account with the reading date, the meter serial number, the previous reading, the current reading and the reason code.

7.5 Customers must be notified of any adjustment exceeding £50.00 within five working days of posting, using template BL-14.

7.6 EXCEPTION: Clauses 7.1 to 7.3 do not apply where the meter is inaccessible due to a documented access refusal logged by Field Operations. In such cases the billing team must issue a written request for access under template BL-19 and may continue billing on estimate for no more than three further periods.

7.7 EXCEPTION: Where a customer is registered under the Priority Services Register, adjustments under 7.3 may be applied in instalments over up to six billing periods at the discretion of a Billing Team Leader, provided the customer has been informed in writing.

7.8 Corrections to a previously issued adjustment must be logged as a new entry and must reference the original entry number. The original entry must not be altered or deleted.

Policy ref: HCL-RES-07 | Version 3.2 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Branch Services Manager

1. Scope
1.1 This policy applies to reservations placed on lending stock through the Libra Reserve system at all branches, including Eastgate, Mill Road and Quayside.

2. Reservation limits
2.1 A member in good standing may hold up to 15 active reservations at any one time.
2.2 A reservation expires if the item has not been collected within 7 calendar days of the notification date.
2.3 Items reserved for interlibrary loan are excluded from clause 2.2 and expire after 21 calendar days.

3. Fines and blocks
3.1 Members with fines totalling £10.00 or more may not place new reservations.
3.2 Where outstanding fines are just under £10.00, the branch librarian may place a provisional hold of up to 3 working days pending payment.

4. Exceptions
4.1 A branch librarian may extend a reservation expiry by up to 7 days where the member has a documented reason for non-collection, such as hospital admission or bereavement.
4.2 Clause 3.1 does not apply to members under 16 years of age. Fines for these members are recorded but do not block reservations.
4.3 Any extension under clause 4.1 beyond 14 days requires approval from the Branch Services Manager and must be entered in the member record note field.

4.7 Estimates shall not be issued to a supply point with a registered smart meter that has reported successfully in the preceding 30 days.

SR01 Access not available

Facilities Policy FP-07: Out-of-Hours Plant Callouts and Cost Authorisation
Issue 4 (effective 1 September 2026). Supersedes Issue 3 dated 14 March 2025.

Scope
This policy applies to all reactive plant callouts logged through the Helpdesk for Blocks A to D, Quayside Court, including the basement plant room and the rooftop AHU compound.

Definitions
1.1 "Out-of-hours" means any time outside 07:30 to 18:00 Monday to Friday, and all day on public holidays.
1.2 "Callout cap" means the maximum sum a contractor may invoice for a single reactive attendance without written variation approval from the Facilities Manager.
1.3 "Work order" means the Helpdesk reference issued at the point of logging, in the format HD-26-XXXXX.

Authorisation
2.1 Contractors may attend out-of-hours faults on the Helpdesk's instruction alone.
2.2 Where the estimated cost of work exceeds the callout cap of £650.00 (excluding VAT), the contractor must submit a variation request through the Helpdesk within two working hours of attendance.
2.3 The Facilities Manager shall approve or reject a variation request within one working day.
2.4 A variation approved by telephone must be confirmed in writing on the same day and attached to the work order.

Exceptions
3.1 Clause 2.2 does not apply to life-safety faults, including loss of smoke ventilation, fire alarm panel faults, and lift entrapment. Such work may proceed immediately, and the variation request must be raised within the following working day.
3.2 Clause 2.4 does not apply where the Facilities Manager is unavailable for more than four hours. In that case the duty engineer's written record of the instruction is sufficient.

Records
4.1 Each work order must record the time of logging, the time of attendance, and the time of completion.
4.2 Invoices quoting a work order without a matching variation record will be held until reconciled.

Case note: HD-26-04417 (Block C, rooftop AHU 3)
Logged 22 October 2026 at 17:42 by the building manager, Ruth Adeyemi-Clarke, after tenants on floor 6 reported no air movement. Contractor Brightwater Mechanical attended at 18:25 and isolated a seized supply fan bearing. The Helpdesk initially recorded the callout cap estimate as £560.00, but the engineer's sheet, dated 23 October, gives a revised estimate of £1,065.00 for the replacement motor and bearing assembly, excluding VAT.

Ruth Adeyemi-Clarke states that the fault was not life-safety related and that the variation was raised only after the work had started, at 19:10. Duty engineer Callum Osei states that smoke ventilation on floor 6 was reported as affected at the time of attendance and that he rang the Facilities Manager at 18:50, receiving verbal approval. The Facilities Manager's log for that evening shows no call received after 18:00 and no approval recorded.

Related references on file: HD-26-04391 (Block A, lift 2 door sensor, £212.40); HD-26-04428 (Block D, boiler flue inspection, £1,480.00 quoted, not yet approved); purchase order PO-88213 raised 23 October, value £1,065.00; prior variation VR-26-0112 dated 3 March 2026.

Depot Operations Manual, Section 7: Vehicle Reallocation During Service Disruption
Policy reference: DOM-7.4 | Version 3.2 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Head of Depot Operations

7.4.1 Scope
This clause applies where a scheduled vehicle is withdrawn from route by the Control Room and a replacement must be assigned from the depot pool.

7.4.2 Vehicle classes
Standard (Class S) vehicles may substitute for Class S or Class H (hybrid) duties. Class H vehicles may substitute for Class H duties only. Articulated (Class A) vehicles may substitute for any duty on routes 14, 22 and 31.

7.4.3 Priority order
Where more than one vehicle is available, the allocator shall assign in the following order: (a) vehicles with a valid Certificate of Fitness due within 14 days shall not be assigned to duties exceeding 6 hours; (b) vehicles with the lowest cumulative mileage since last scheduled service; (c) vehicles returned from workshop most recently.

7.4.4 Driver hours
No vehicle shall be assigned where the rostered driver would exceed 9 hours on duty without a 45-minute break, per Clause 5.2.

7.4.5 Recording
Every reallocation shall be logged in the Control Room Dispatch Log (CRDL) with the withdrawal time, reason code, replacement vehicle fleet number and time of confirmation.

7.4.6 Exception: Weekend and bank holiday duties
Clauses 7.4.3(c) and 7.4.4 do not apply to duties operating between 22:00 on a Friday and 05:00 on the following Monday, where the Duty Manager may assign any available vehicle that meets 7.4.2, provided the assignment is recorded with reason code EX-7.

7.4.7 Exception: Month-end maintenance window
Vehicles scheduled for the month-end inspection cycle (last three working days of each calendar month) are unavailable for reallocation unless the Head of Depot Operations approves in writing.

---

INCIDENT REPORT: EXPENSES DESK

Reference: EXP-IR-2026-0417
Report type: Duplicate card transaction / receipt mismatch
Raised by: Priyanka Oduya, Expenses Desk Analyst
Date raised: Tuesday 27 October 2026
Business unit: Strategy & Transformation, Leeds office
Cost centre: CC-4420
Card holder: Tobias Wrenfield (corporate card ending 7713)

1. Background

This report covers a claim submitted on Friday 23 October for a client dinner held at the Halden Quay restaurant, Leeds, on Thursday 22 October. I am writing this up in some detail because the claim has been bounced twice and I want the trail to be readable for whoever picks it up next, including Sanjay in finance business partnering, who asked for it last week when the first query came in. Apologies for the length, it got away from me a bit.

2. Timeline (all times local, UK)

Thu 22 Oct, 19:42. Table of six booked under Wrenfield, party confirmed by the restaurant's booking system as six covers, deposit not taken.
Thu 22 Oct, 21:58. Card payment authorised at the terminal, GBP 486.40, reference HQ-22103.
Thu 22 Oct, 22:14. Second authorisation attempted on the same terminal, declined by the issuer as a duplicate, no funds moved.
Fri 23 Oct, 09:05. Wrenfield submits expense claim EXP-88412 for GBP 486.40, receipt attached (photo, slightly cut off at the bottom).
Fri 23 Oct, 16:30. Claim auto-flagged by the duplicate-merchant rule because of the declined attempt. Held in queue.
Sat 24 Oct, 11:20. Wrenfield emails the desk from his phone, says the card was only charged once and the flag is wrong. Email is not picked up until Monday.
Mon 26 Oct, 08:47. I review the claim and request the itemised receipt from the restaurant through the portal.
Mon 26 Oct, 15:12. Restaurant sends a PDF. Subtotal GBP 412.00, service charge GBP 41.20, VAT GBP 33.20 is not shown separately, total GBP 486.40 as above. The restaurant also notes a manual correction to a bottle line, which I have not yet been able to reconcile.
Mon 26 Oct, 17:45. Claim returned to Wrenfield with a request for a corrected receipt.
Tue 27 Oct, 10:03. Wrenfield replies (see section 3).

3. Witness and participant remarks

Wrenfield, by email, 27 Oct, 10:03: "I was there, I paid, it was one bottle of the Rioja on the list, maybe two, I genuinely do not remember and the kids were on a call with my wife at the time so I was distracted. Honestly the 486.40 is what I'd put in, I don't know why the sheet says anything else, it was a long night and Halden were brilliant about the table and I'd rather not hold the team up over a receipt. Happy to sign whatever you need."

Restaurant duty manager (phone note, Mon 26 Oct, 15:30, recorded by me): confirms the table, confirms a single authorisation, says the bottle correction was made at the table by the server and the original figure on the first printed bill was GBP 448.00 before a re-run.

Note from the initial desk entry, Fri 23 Oct, typed by the intake agent: "Total 448.00 per guest bill, treat as provisional."

4. Figure

The claim total was first entered at GBP 448.00 on intake, taken from the provisional bill noted above. On review against the restaurant's PDF and the authorisation record, the correct total is GBP 486.40. The GBP 448.00 figure should be disregarded and the claim amended accordingly.

5. Current status

Claim EXP-88412 remains in the held queue. The duplicate flag has not been cleared. No payment has been released. The bottle correction is still outstanding and the restaurant has said it will send the server's amended slip on request.

Policy Extract: PRO-POL-07 Low-Value Tenders and Quotations
Version 3.2 | Effective 1 August 2026 | Owner: Head of Procurement Operations

7. Thresholds and quotations

7.1 Any requirement with an estimated total contract value of £25,000 or more (excluding VAT) must follow the formal tender route in Section 8.

7.2 Requirements with an estimated value of at least £5,000 but below £25,000 require written quotations from a minimum of three suppliers, recorded on Form PF-4 (Quotation Record).

7.3 Estimated value is calculated over the full contract term, including any optional extensions. Requirements must not be divided into separate orders to fall below a threshold.

7.4 Where a requisition is raised with an estimate within £1,000 of a threshold in 7.1 or 7.2, the requester must attach a written cost build-up, and the Head of Procurement Operations must confirm the estimate before a purchase order is issued.

7.5 Exception – sole source. Where only one supplier can meet a specification, the requester may proceed with a single quotation regardless of value, provided Form PF-7 (Sole Source Justification) is signed by the budget holder and countersigned by the evaluation panel chair.

7.6 Exception – emergency. Purchases required to prevent immediate risk to health, safety or building integrity may be placed without quotations. The budget holder must report the purchase to Procurement Services within two working days.

7.7 An evaluation panel shall consist of no fewer than four members, at least 60 per cent of whom must be academic or professional staff from outside the requesting department.

7.8 Quotations received after the closing time stated on the request are not to be considered, unless the requester records a justified delay on Form PF-4 and the panel chair approves its inclusion.

Reception and Triage Procedures Manual
Section 4: Return Visits and Repeat Attendance
Reference: NWCC-RT-04 (Rev. 7)
Effective: 1 March 2026

4.1 Scope. This section applies to any patient presenting at the reception desk for a second or subsequent attendance for the same complaint, or for a result, dressing or suture review, within the periods set out below. Reception staff must record the first attendance date on the triage sheet before passing the patient to the triage nurse.

4.2 Return window. A repeat attendance is classed as a "return" where the patient's previous attendance for the same complaint ended no more than five (5) working days before the current attendance. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays observed in the county.

4.3 Fast-track. A returning patient may be seen on the fast-track list without re-registration, provided the triage nurse has recorded the previous clinician's name.

4.4 Exception: wound and suture review. Patients returning for suture removal or wound review within ten (10) calendar days of discharge are not subject to clause 4.2. These are booked directly by the discharging clinician and do not require triage.

4.5 Where the triage sheet "Previous discharge date / time" field is blank, the patient must be treated as a first attendance and the nurse must note the omission in the free-text box.

08:52 Pre-anaesthetic bloods taken by Kieran Vos, veterinary nurse. Sample sent to in-house analyser.

09:40 Anaesthetic depth adjusted and fluid bolus of 10 ml/kg started.
09:58 Heart rate returned to 124 bpm. Procedure continued.
10:45 Extraction completed. Patient recovered in ICU kennel under observation.
11:20 Owner telephoned by Gemma Ferrand. Owner advised of minor complication.

3. Leak allowance eligibility

3.1 A domestic customer may apply for a one-off leak allowance where a concealed or underground supply pipe leak on the customer's side of the boundary stop tap has been repaired by a registered plumber, and the repair invoice is dated within 42 days of the date the leak was first reported to us.

3.2 The allowance is calculated on the excess consumption recorded between the last actual meter read before the leak was reported and the first actual meter read after the repair date, less the customer's average consumption for the same period in the previous year. Where no previous-year figure exists, the assessor shall use the regional domestic average of 0.31 cubic metres per day per resident.

3.3 Allowances are paid as a credit against the next bill. Cash payments are made only where the account is closed.

3.4 The assessor must record the meter serial number, the reading taken at report, and the reading taken at repair on form LA-2 before any allowance is calculated.

4. Exceptions

4.1 Clause 3.1 does not apply where the leak is reported more than 42 days after the repair invoice date, unless the customer provides a written statement from the plumber confirming the leak was active during the period in question.

4.2 Where the meter has been found to be stopped, reversed or unreadable, the assessor may accept a customer's own photographic reading if it is supported by a timestamped image. Estimated reads are not accepted under this exception.

4.3 Clause 3.2 is varied for properties with more than four registered occupants: the regional average is multiplied by the number of occupants, to a maximum of 1.20 cubic metres per day.

PR-SC-07.1 Scope. This section applies to all tenders for goods and services with an estimated total contract value between £10,000 and £75,000 (excluding VAT) where the requisitioning department has not requested a full open procedure.

PR-SC-07.2 Minimum response period. Bidders shall be allowed no fewer than ten (10) working days from the date of issue to submit a response. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays observed in England and Wales.

PR-SC-07.3 Evaluation panel. Each panel shall have no fewer than three members, one of whom shall be the evaluation panel chair. The chair shall not have a financial interest in any bidder.

PR-SC-07.4 Scoring. Each evaluator shall score each response against the published criteria on a scale of 0 to 10. Individual scores shall be recorded to one decimal place. Where the award criterion is quality, the quality score shall be the arithmetic mean of the individual evaluator scores, rounded to two decimal places.

PR-SC-07.5 Delivery information. Bidders shall state the lead time for delivery in working days from receipt of a purchase order. Where a bidder states lead time in calendar weeks, the procurement team shall convert it at five working days per week.

PR-SC-07.6 Service history. Bidders shall provide, for the preceding twelve months, the number of service calls received and the number of scheduled visits completed. The service reliability ratio is calculated as calls received divided by scheduled visits completed.

PR-SC-07.7 Exception: urgent requirements. The response period in PR-SC-07.2 may be reduced to five (5) working days where the Director of Estates certifies in writing that a delay would expose persons or property to risk. The certificate shall be filed with the tender record.

PR-SC-07.8 Exception: sole-source. Where only one supplier can meet the specification, PR-SC-07.2 to PR-SC-07.4 do not apply. A sole-source justification form (Form PS-14) shall be approved by the Head of Procurement Operations.

2.1 A fault is classed as Category B where one or more doors fail to release after a valid code is entered, or where the keypad registers fewer than 90 per cent of key presses in the diagnostic cycle.
2.2 A fault is classed as Category A where a door is held open for longer than 45 seconds, or where the bank controller reports a power interruption exceeding 3 minutes.

3. Response times
3.1 Category A faults must be attended within 4 working hours of logging.
3.2 Category B faults must be attended within 1 working day of logging. Attendance is recorded when the technician scans the bank QR plate on site.

4. Service credits
4.1 A service credit of £18.50 per affected door per calendar day is payable to the network partner where a Category B fault remains open beyond the window in clause 3.2.
4.2 Credits are capped at £140.00 per bank per calendar month.
4.3 Exception: where the delay is caused by a parts backorder notified in writing to the partner before the window expires, clause 4.1 does not apply for the period of the backorder.

5.1 Technicians may open a bank cabinet only with a logged work order number.

Section 4: Small Tenders

4.1 A tender is classed as a small tender where the estimated total contract value, excluding VAT, is below £25,000 and the contract term does not exceed 36 months.

Section 5: Supplier Performance Review

5.1 Each supplier on a live framework is reviewed at the end of each quarter. Performance is measured as a service failure rate, being the number of logged service failures divided by the number of service requests raised in the quarter, expressed as a percentage.

5.2 A service failure rate of 2.0% or above in any quarter triggers a formal review under clause 5.4.

5.3 Failures attributable to the university's own timetable changes, cancelled client requests, or force majeure are excluded from the count.

5.4 A formal review shall be chaired by the Head of Procurement Services and shall conclude within 15 working days of the quarter end.

5.5 Exception: where a supplier has been reviewed under clause 5.4 in either of the two preceding quarters and the failure rate has since fallen below 2.0%, the Head of Procurement Services may, at their discretion, defer the review by one quarter and record the reason on the supplier file.

Section 6: Records

6.1 Supplier files shall be retained for six years from the date of contract expiry, in line with the university's records schedule (ref. RS-2019-044).

Policy LAN-POL-07.3: Outdoor Play and Indoor Temperature Monitoring (version 4, reviewed 14 September 2026)

7.3.1 Indoor room temperature must be recorded at 08:30, 11:00 and 14:30 each day using the wall-mounted thermometer in each room, and the reading entered on the Room Log sheet with initials.

7.3.2 Where any recorded reading exceeds 24.0°C, the room leader must move the group to the garden or the shaded verandah, open the high-level windows, and inform the Deputy Manager within 15 minutes.

This clause applies to all sea (FCL and LCL) and road consignments booked through the Southampton and Felixstowe desks.

(a) A late tender may be rebooked onto the next available sailing provided the shipper confirms in writing within three (3) working days of the original cut-off.
(b) Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and English bank holidays.
(c) Confirmations received after the third working day lapse and the booking is closed.

4.7.4 Exception: documented port delay
Where a terminal, customs or port authority has issued a written hold notice, clause 4.7.3(a) is extended by the number of working days the hold remained in force, up to a maximum of five (5) working days. The hold notice must be attached to the booking record before the extension is applied.

4.7.5 Storage charges
Storage is charged at £38.50 per TEU per day for each day beyond the free period of four (4) calendar days. Storage accrued during a valid hold under 4.7.4 is not chargeable to the shipper.

Each late tender must carry a completed HV-LT/2 with the time of receipt, the name of the receiving clerk and the reference of any hold notice.

7.1.1 This clause applies to all children attending Bramble Hill, including those in the Acorns, Willow and Juniper rooms.

7. Temperature excursions

7.1 A temperature excursion is any period during which product temperature, as recorded by a calibrated logger in the load or at the dock probe point, is outside its storage band for longer than the tolerance in clause 7.3.

7.2 Loggers shall record at intervals not exceeding 10 minutes. Logger serial numbers are recorded on the Load Release Sheet (Form HCL-LRS-3).

7.3 Tolerance. Chilled product may remain above +5 C for up to 45 minutes cumulative per load. Frozen product may not exceed -15 C for any period.

7.4 Each excursion shall be logged in the Excursion Register within one working hour of detection, stating the logger ID, start time, end time, peak reading and the duty manager's name.

7.5 Any load with an excursion over tolerance is placed on QA hold. The load shall not be released until a disposition is recorded by a QA technician.

7.6 Exception: dock door events. Where an excursion occurs solely because a dock door is open during loading or unloading, and the total open time does not exceed 20 minutes, the excursion is excluded from the tolerance in clause 7.3 provided that the door-open event is recorded on the dock log (Form HCL-DL-1) with a signature from the shift supervisor. The exclusion does not apply to weekend or bank-holiday operations unless a second signature from the on-call QA technician is also obtained.

7.7 Carrier units without a recording logger are not eligible for release under any exception in this clause.

7.8 Dispositions are recorded as RELEASE, DOWNGRADE or DESTROY. Dispositions of DESTROY require countersignature by the Head of Quality Assurance or deputy.

Policy extract: PRT/07 (Rev. 3)
Issued by: Clinical Governance Office
Effective: 1 September 2026

Section 4: Out-of-hours repeat prescriptions and controlled items

4.1 Repeat prescription requests received at reception must be logged on the Repeat Request Register (form RRR-2) with date, time received, patient NHS number, item, strength and quantity requested.

4.2 Requests for medicines listed in Schedule 3 of the Clinic Formulary (controlled and high-risk items) must not be issued by reception staff under any circumstances.

4.3 The 48-hour rule applies. A repeat request may be actioned by the duty clinician only where the last issue date recorded on the patient record is at least 48 hours before the time of request. Where the interval is less than 48 hours, the request is referred to the duty clinician for review.

4.4 Interval calculations must use the timestamp of the last issue as recorded in the dispensing log, not the date printed on the original slip.

4.5 Exception: where a patient is recorded on the Palliative Care List (PCL) the 48-hour rule in 4.3 does not apply. Requests may be actioned at any time on production of the PCL reference number, which must be written on RRR-2.

4.6 Exception: a single emergency supply of up to 7 days of a non-controlled item may be issued by the duty clinician on a weekend or public holiday where the patient cannot attend in person, provided the supply is entered on the dispensing log before the end of the shift.

4.7 Weekend and bank holiday requests received after 18:00 on Friday are held until 08:00 the following working day unless flagged urgent by a clinician.

4.8 Staff must not alter the recorded issue date to make an interval appear compliant.

Recorded by: H. Dunmore, Receptionist (Band 3)
Patient: NHS 472 018 3396, DOB 14/03/1961
Item: Amlodipine 10mg tablets, qty 28

Request received Friday 23/10/2026 at 17:42. Patient states the previous supply was collected from the pharmacy at 09:15 on Monday 19/10/2026 and that the supply has run out early because of a dosing change at home. Dispensing log shows last issue timestamp 19/10/2026 09:15, batch AM-4471.

Patient has a PCL reference recorded on the record but reference was not written on RRR-2 at time of call. Patient also asked whether a second item, Bendroflumethiazide 2.5mg, could be added. Staff note that this item is not on the patient's current repeat template.

Call transferred to duty clinician line at 17:55. Voicemail left for Dr. A. Okonkwo at 18:20. Patient informed the request is being reviewed and that no supply has been issued at time of writing.

Dispensing & Prescription Collection Policy
Document ref: DCP-07 (rev. 4)
Owner: Responsible Pharmacist, Dispensing Desk
Effective: 1 September 2026
Review date: 1 March 2027

1. Scope
1.1 This policy applies to all NHS and private prescriptions presented at the collection desk, including repeat dispensing items and owing slips.
1.2 Staff must read this policy alongside SOP-14 (Controlled Drugs Register) and the Medicines Storage Procedure, ref. MSP-03.

2. Ready-for-collection holding period
2.1 Dispensed items are held in the bagged-prescription bay for a maximum of 14 days from the date of dispensing.
2.2 Items not collected within that period are returned to stock, and the pharmacy record is annotated "not collected – returned" with the initials of the member of staff who processed the return.
2.3 Items containing Schedule 2 or Schedule 3 controlled drugs are held for 7 days only and are then returned to the dispensary for destruction checks.

3. Identity and authority to collect
3.1 The patient, or a named nominee recorded on the patient profile, must collect the medicine. Staff must check date of birth or photo identification before handing over any Schedule 2 or Schedule 3 item.
3.2 Collection by a third party who is not a recorded nominee requires the responsible pharmacist's approval and a signed authorisation form (Form CD-9b).

4. Exceptions
4.1 Where a patient is admitted to hospital or is housebound, the responsible pharmacist may extend the holding period for a non-controlled item by up to 21 days, provided the extension is noted on the bag label and the pharmacy record.
4.2 An extension under clause 4.1 does not apply to Schedule 2 or Schedule 3 items, which remain subject to clause 2.3 in all cases.
4.3 Any extension must be recorded with the date of the extension, the reason given, and the name of the person who authorised it.

5. Recording
5.1 Each collection is recorded on the dispensing system with the date, time, and collector's name. Times are entered in 24-hour format.
5.2 Discrepancies between the bag label and the register must be reported to the responsible pharmacist before the item is released.

7. Catch Quota Allocation and Overage

7.1 Each member vessel is allocated a seasonal quota of demersal landings in tonnes, as set out in the annual allocation schedule issued by the Board.

7.2 Quota balances are calculated from landing declarations received at the landing office and not from skipper estimates.

7.3 A vessel is treated as approaching quota when its cumulative landings reach 90% of its allocation. Landing office staff shall notify the vessel's skipper in writing at that point.

7.4 Where cumulative landings exceed allocation, the excess shall be deducted from the following season's allocation at the rate of 1.15 tonnes for every tonne of overage.

7.5 Exception: A vessel may apply to the Quota Committee for overage to be deducted at 1.00 tonne per tonne where the overage arises from a documented weighbridge fault, a recorded engine or refrigeration breakdown, or a storm recorded in the harbour master's log.

7.6 Applications under 7.5 must be lodged within 14 days of the date of the final landing declaration concerned.

Customer Billing Policy BP-14: Estimated Bills, Meter Readings and Back-Billing
Version 3.2 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Customer Billing Team, Leeds

1. Scope
1.1 This policy applies to all domestic and small business accounts billed on a monthly or quarterly cycle.

2. Meter readings
2.1 Customers should submit a meter reading through the online portal or the automated phone line between the 20th and the last day of each billing month.
2.2 Where no actual reading has been received for 90 days or more, the billing system will issue an estimated bill.
2.3 An estimated bill must not exceed the customer's average daily consumption over the previous 12 months multiplied by the number of days in the billing period.

3. Back-billing
3.1 Where an actual reading shows consumption above the amount billed, the difference may be back-billed for up to 12 months from the date of the reading.
3.2 Back-billed amounts above £300.00 must be approved by a Billing Team Leader before issue.
3.3 Customers must be offered a payment plan of no fewer than 6 and no more than 18 monthly instalments.

4. Exceptions
4.1 Clause 3.1 does not apply where the supplier failed to obtain a reading for reasons attributable to the supplier, including a reader appointment cancelled by the supplier.

7.1 Scope

7.2.1 Where the quantity invoiced exceeds the quantity received, the Buyer of record shall raise a short-delivery claim within five (5) working days of the goods receipt date.
7.2.2 The adjustment value is calculated as the invoiced unit price multiplied by the shortfall quantity, plus any freight charged on the short-delivered lines pro rata to value.
7.2.3 Adjustments under £250.00 may be processed by the AP Team Leader without further approval.

7.3 Credit note matching
7.3.1 A supplier credit note must quote the original invoice number. Credit notes received without an invoice reference are held in suspense account 2990 for no longer than twenty (20) working days.
7.3.2 Corrected credit notes supersede earlier versions only where the earlier version has been formally withdrawn by the supplier in writing. Verbal corrections are not accepted.

7.4.1 Clauses 7.2.1 and 7.2.3 do not apply where the supplier is on the watch list maintained under Section 11, in which case all adjustments require sign-off by the Supplier Relations Manager.
7.4.2 Clause 7.2.1 is extended to ten (10) working days where the shortfall is notified by the receiving site during a planned shutdown.

7.5 Record keeping
Claims, credit notes and approvals are to be retained in the AP archive for seven (7) years from the end of the financial year to which they relate.

7.3.1 Scope. This guidance applies to claims under the Home Contents Essentials and Home Contents Plus policy wordings where the loss arises from water escaping from a fixed installation at the insured property.

7.3.2 Evidence. The handler shall obtain at least two of the following: a plumber's invoice, a photograph of the affected area dated before repair, or a moisture reading taken within 72 hours of notification.

7.3.3 Settlement limit. Contents claims for water damage to floor coverings are subject to a sub-limit of £2,400 per incident unless an endorsement states otherwise.

7.3.4 Exception. Clause 7.3.3 does not apply where the insured has a current maintenance certificate for the installation issued within the previous 12 months.

7.3.5 Disputed facts. Where the insured and a third party give conflicting accounts of when water was first noticed, the handler shall record both accounts verbatim and refer the file to a technical assessor before any offer is made.

AP-POL-07 Rev. 3: Goods Receipt Variance and Invoice Hold Procedure
Effective 1 March 2026. Approved by: R. Okonedo, Financial Controller

7.1 Purpose
This clause sets out how Accounts Payable treats supplier invoices where the invoiced quantity or value differs from the goods receipt note (GRN) or purchase order (PO).

7.2 Tolerance
Invoices within a variance of 2.0% of PO value, or £150.00, whichever is the lower, may be approved by the AP Team Leader without further reference.

7.3 Hold
Any invoice outside the tolerance in 7.2 is placed on hold (status HOLD-VAR) and referred to the budget holder named on the PO.

7.4 Exception: Consignment Stock
Where the supplier is recorded on the Vendor Master with consignment flag = Y, variance tolerance in 7.2 does not apply. Invoices are matched to the consumption report issued under SC-CONS-02 and released on the first working day after receipt of that report.

7.5 Exception: Expedited Freight
Freight invoices raised against a PO marked EXPEDITE are exempt from 7.3 where the approving director has signed the expedite authorisation form (FORM AP-EX-2). The form reference must be recorded in the PO notes field.

7.6 Time Limit
Held invoices must be resolved within 10 working days of the hold date. Items unresolved after this period are escalated to the Financial Controller.

Section 3: Leak allowance eligibility

3.1 A leak allowance may be considered where a customer reports a suspected concealed leak on the customer-side supply pipe and the leak is confirmed by a Harrowmere field engineer.

3.2 The allowance is calculated on the excess consumption above the customer's baseline. The baseline is the mean daily consumption for the 90 days preceding the reported leak, expressed in cubic metres (m³), rounded to two decimal places.

3.3 The excess consumption is the difference between the metered reading at the date of repair and the metered reading at the date the leak was first reported, less the baseline multiplied by the number of days between those two dates.

3.4 Allowances are credited at the tariff rate of £1.84 per m³ in effect on the date the repair is confirmed. Credits below £5.00 are not issued and are carried to the next billing cycle.

3.5 Where the reported leak is confirmed to be on the Harrowmere-owned communication pipe, no allowance is payable under this section.

Section 4: Exceptions

4.1 Clause 3.2 does not apply to customers registered on the Priority Services Register, for whom the baseline shall be set at 0.35 m³ per day regardless of the 90-day mean.

4.2 Where a repair visit is delayed beyond 5 working days by reason of Harrowmere access failure, the reporting date shall be taken as the date of the first failed visit, not the date of the original report.

4.3 Allowances exceeding 180 kg of recovered water equivalent (as recorded on Form LA-7) require sign-off by the Billing Adviser before credit. Forms weighing more than 2 lb in printed copy are to be scanned rather than posted.

5.1 The Billing Adviser shall record each decision on the case management system within two working days, quoting the case reference (format LA-YYYY-NNNNN).

4.1 Purpose
4.1.1 This section sets out the approval levels, matching requirements and exception handling that apply to supplier invoices received at the Stockport and Wakefield sites.

4.2 Approval thresholds
4.2.1 Invoices up to and including GBP 4,999.99 may be approved by a Team Leader, AP.
4.2.2 Invoices from GBP 5,000.00 up to and including GBP 24,999.99 require approval by an AP Manager.

4.3 Three-way match
4.3.1 Each invoice shall be matched to a purchase order and a goods received note (GRN) before payment is released.
4.3.2 Quantities on the invoice must not exceed the GRN quantity by more than 2%.
4.3.3 Price variances up to 1.5% of the PO unit price may be accepted by the AP Manager without re-approval.

4.4.1 Bulk steel supplier invoices are matched on net weight recorded at the weighbridge, in kilograms (kg).
4.4.2 Where the weighbridge ticket is in pounds (lb), the clerk shall convert at 1 lb = 0.4536 kg before matching.
4.4.3 Freight charges are accepted up to 6.5 hours of driver time per load, or the equivalent recorded in the carrier's log.

4.5 Exceptions
4.5.1 Clause 4.2.2 does not apply to invoices from suppliers on the Approved Consignment List (ACL) where a standing approval reference is recorded on the PO. Such invoices may be approved by a Team Leader, AP up to GBP 9,999.99.

Operations Policy OP-14: Consignment Weight Variance and Re-Rating
Revision 3 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Operations Manager

1. Scope
1.1 This policy applies to all sea and road consignments booked under a Halvorsen tariff, including part loads and consolidated LCL shipments.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Declared weight" means the gross weight entered on the booking at confirmation.
2.2 "Verified weight" means the weight recorded on the origin weighbridge ticket or terminal gate weight.
2.3 "Variance" means verified weight less declared weight, expressed in kilograms.

3. Re-rating
3.1 Where variance exceeds 250 kg, the booking shall be re-rated at the applicable tariff band.
3.2 Re-rating shall be notified to the shipper within one (1) working day of receipt of the verified weight.

4. Exceptions
4.1 Clause 3.1 does not apply where the variance arises from dunnage or pallet tare recorded on the packing list dated before collection.
4.2 Consignments under the Priority Road service (ref. PRS-2) are excluded from clause 3.1 where the shipper has accepted the flat-rate surcharge of GBP 85.00.

5.1 The absence trigger points for formal review are as follows:

**Lumen Rides Ltd: Rider Support Policy**
**RSP-14: Refunds and Fare Adjustments**
Version 3.2. Effective 2 October 2026. Owner: Rider Support Operations, Northgate office.

**1. Scope**

1.1 This policy applies to refund requests from riders where the charged fare differs from the metered fare recorded in the trip ledger.

1.2 Agents must not promise a refund before the trip record has been reviewed.

**2. Eligibility**

2.1 A refund may be issued where the charged fare exceeds the metered fare by more than £2.00.

2.2 A claim must be lodged within 14 days of the trip end timestamp. The trip end timestamp is the dropoff time recorded by the driver app, converted to local time.

2.3 Fare components are assessed separately: base fare, distance charge, time charge, booking fee, surcharges and waiting fees.

**3. Waiting fees**

3.1 Waiting time is chargeable only after the free waiting allowance has elapsed. The allowance is 4 minutes.
*Revision note: 3.1 previously read "5 minutes". Corrected 9 October 2026 following Pricing Ticket PT-2291.*

3.2 Waiting fees are charged at £0.30 per minute, rounded down to the whole minute.

**4. Exceptions**

4.1 Clause 2.2 does not apply where the driver has logged a safety incident against the trip. In those cases the claim window is 30 days from the trip end timestamp.

4.2 Where a trip was booked as a multi-stop journey, each stop is assessed under clause 2.3 as a separate line, and the booking fee is not refundable in part.

**5. Evidence**

5.1 Where a rider disputes a waiting fee, the driver's arrival photograph and location trace are the primary evidence. Agents must confirm that the photo set is complete. A complete set is the number of photographs listed in the booking record.

Section 7: Temperature Excursions and Load Release
Policy Extract CC-7.3 (Rev. 4, effective 1 September 2026)

7.3.1 Scope
This clause applies to all chilled (0°C to +5°C) and frozen (−18°C or below) loads leaving the Hadleigh and Wrexham cross-dock sites, including multi-drop vehicles.

7.3.2 Probe readings
Each load shall be probed at dispatch using a calibrated probe thermometer. The core reading shall be recorded on the Dispatch Release Sheet (form DRS-2) in the "Core °C" field. Readings taken from the vehicle air supply are not acceptable as a core reading.

7.3.3 Excursion threshold
A load is in excursion when any product core reading exceeds its band by more than 2.0°C for a cumulative period of 30 minutes or longer. Cumulative time shall be logged from the data logger in hours and minutes (hh:mm), not as decimal hours.

7.3.4 Dispatcher action on excursion
Where an excursion is identified before departure, the dispatcher shall:
(a) place the load on hold in WMS status "QA-HOLD";
(b) notify the Duty Quality Officer within 15 minutes of identification;
(c) not release the load until a written disposition is recorded on DRS-2.

7.3.5 Exception: short-term excursion on frozen stock
Frozen loads may be released without QA-HOLD where the core reading is no higher than −15°C, the cumulative excursion is less than 45 minutes, and the Duty Quality Officer has approved release by telephone. Approval shall be recorded on DRS-2 with the officer's staff number.

7.3.6 Exception does not apply to
(a) chilled loads containing raw poultry, minced meat or shellfish;
(b) loads carrying a customer temperature certificate;
(c) any load where the data logger has failed or shows gaps longer than 10 minutes.

7.3.7 Record retention
DRS-2 forms and data logger downloads shall be retained for 36 months from the date of dispatch.

BA-7.1 Scope
This section applies to annual and monthly subscriptions to the Brightwater Pro, Brightwater Team and Brightwater Enterprise plans, billed in GBP, EUR or USD.

BA-7.2 Service credit eligibility
A customer is eligible for a service credit where a verified service incident has lasted longer than 4 consecutive hours within the billing period and the incident is recorded in the Status Register under a reference beginning SR-.

BA-7.3 Credit calculation
The credit equals the pro-rata monthly fee for the affected seats multiplied by 0.05 for each full 4-hour block beyond the first, up to a maximum of 0.25 of the monthly fee. Credits are rounded down to the nearest penny.

BA-7.4 Dispute window
A customer may raise a subscription dispute within 15 working days of the invoice date. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and English bank holidays. The Account Manager must acknowledge the dispute within 2 working days of receipt.

BA-7.5 Refund approval
Refunds up to £500.00 may be approved by an Account Manager. Refunds above £500.00 and up to £2,500.00 require approval from the Billing Operations Lead. Refunds above £2,500.00 require approval from the Finance Director.

BA-7.6 Exception: prior written waiver
Notwithstanding BA-7.4, a dispute raised after the window closes shall be accepted where the customer holds a written waiver issued under Form BA-F9 by a Billing Operations Lead and the waiver is dated within the 90 calendar days preceding the invoice date. Waivers issued by any other role are not valid for this purpose.

BA-7.7 Record keeping
All credit and refund decisions must be logged in the Billing Ledger with the Status Register reference, the invoice number and the approving role.

7. Recording and counting of landed weight

7.1 Every landing of quota-managed species shall be recorded on a landing slip (Form LS-4) at the time of weighing. Each slip shall show vessel registration, member number, date, species, net weight in kilograms, and the scale identifier.

7.2 The landed weight for a trip is the sum of the net weights on all LS-4 slips raised for that trip, including replacement slips issued under clause 7.4.

7.3 Landed weight is counted against the member's annual allocation as held on the date of landing. Where cumulative landed weight would exceed that allocation, the Landing Officer shall place the vessel on hold and notify the Quota Secretary the same working day.

7.4 Where the landing scale reading differs from the buyer's weighbridge by more than 0.5 kg per 100 kg, the buyer's weighbridge figure applies and a replacement slip shall be raised marked "RE-WEIGH".

7.5 Exception, swapped tonnage. Tonnage received under a swap agreement approved by the Board before the landing date may be added to the allocation for that landing only, provided the swap reference is entered in box 9 of the slip. Swap references take the form SW-2026/nnn.

7.6 Exception, distress landings. Landings made under a distress notice (Form DN-1) shall be recorded and weighed as normal but shall not be counted against allocation until the Board has reviewed the notice. The DN-1 reference shall be entered in box 10 of the slip.

7.7 Scale checks shall be logged on Form SC-2 at the start of each landing day, recording each test-weight reading in kilograms.

7.1 The control room supervisor (CRS) may authorise a relief driver to take over a running service where the rostered driver is delayed by more than 15 minutes.

7.2 Relief drivers must hold a current route familiarisation certificate for the route being covered and must have completed the wheelchair ramp refresher (WRR) within the previous 12 months.

7.3 Each depot shall keep its WRR sign-in sheet current. At the start of each quarter the depot manager shall confirm the number of relief drivers on the depot roster and the number holding a valid WRR, and send both figures to the Operations Office.

7.4 Exception: where no WRR-qualified relief driver can be reached within 45 minutes of the disruption, the CRS may assign an unrefreshed relief driver to a non-accessible service only. The reason must be entered in the incident log at the time of assignment.

Clinical Policy CP-14: Client Estimates and Additional Treatment
Version 3.2 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Policy owner: Practice Manager (J. Okonedo)

4. Additional treatment

4.1 Where a written estimate has been issued, any additional treatment that increases the total cost must be authorised by the owner before it is carried out.

4.2 Re-contact is not required where the revised total does not exceed the original written estimate by more than 15%. Such increases are to be noted on the invoice against reference EST-VAR.

4.3 Exception: where anaesthesia is in progress and a delay would materially compromise the patient, the attending clinician may proceed without re-contact. The reason must be recorded in the clinical notes within 1 hour, and the owner informed at the earliest opportunity.

4.4 Authorisation may be given by telephone, by text message from the registered mobile, or by signed estimate. Verbal authorisation is recorded with the date, time and receptionist initials.

4.5 Where more than one registered owner is listed, the signed authorisation of every co-owner is required unless the record states otherwise.

Preamble. Most of the refund questions that reach the box office are simple, and this section is meant to keep them simple. It is also the section people reach for when a patron has had a bad evening, so please read it all the way through before you quote anybody a number. Yes, the clauses below are a little long. Ruth asked for them to be written out in full after the spring incident with the Tuesday matinee, and nobody has found a shorter way of saying it that doesn't leave a gap somewhere.

4.1 Standard refund window. A patron may request a refund on a ticket for a performance up to and including 48 hours before its start time, subject to clause 4.3.

4.2 Processing fee. A non-refundable booking fee of £2.50 per ticket applies to all refunds. Group bookings of ten or more are charged the fee once per booking, not per seat, as agreed with the Harbourside Group Sales team in January.

4.3 Late requests and exceptions. Requests made less than 48 hours before the performance may be refunded at the discretion of the duty House Manager only where one or more of the following applies: (a) the performance was cancelled or materially altered by the Playhouse; (b) the patron has a medical certificate dated within seven days of the performance; (c) the patron is a bereaved next-of-kin, on production of evidence to the satisfaction of the duty House Manager. Exceptions under (a) do not attract the fee in clause 4.2.

4.4 Accessibility seating. Wheelchair and companion bookings are refunded in full, including the fee, at any time, on the Access Team's confirmation.

4.5 Vouchers. Where a refund is declined under clause 4.3, the patron may be offered a Playhouse credit voucher equal to the ticket face value less the fee. Vouchers expire 12 months from issue, are non-transferable, and are not cash-convertible.

Case note (BO/2026/0917), prepared by Dev Chaudhry, Box Office Supervisor, 22 October 2026.

He asked whether we could return the money in full.

I explained clause 4.1 and that the request fell inside 48 hours. He said he understood, but asked whether a sick child counted as medical. I told him I would check with the duty House Manager. The patron has since emailed a photograph of a GP letter dated 20 October, addressed to his daughter, which describes a gastrointestinal illness and advises her to rest for five days. 4. Notification of absence
4.1 An employee unable to attend work must notify their line manager by telephone or through the Rotaweb absence form no later than 60 minutes before the start of their shift.

5. Recording of episodes
5.1 Each period of absence is recorded as one episode. Episodes separated by fewer than 3 working days are merged into a single episode.
5.2 The Absence Frequency Indicator for a depot is the number of episodes recorded in the review period, divided by the number of rostered shifts in the same period, reported to two decimal places.

6.1 Clause 4.1 does not apply where the employee has been admitted to hospital or referred for emergency treatment. In those cases a family member or representative must notify the depot within 4 hours of admission.

4.4 Documents supplied as scans. Scanned source material is charged at 3 minutes per page for layout preparation, with the cumulative total rounded up to the next full hour for billing. Pages shorter than 40 words are excluded from this calculation.

4.5 Quality threshold. Each freelancer's delivered work is scored by a reviewer on a 0 to 100 scale. A score below 70 on two consecutive assignments triggers a review meeting. Reviewers' scores on the Q3 pilot are recorded in the attached sheet and are provisional.

4.6 Exception: client-held deadlines. Where a client has agreed a fixed delivery date in a signed contract, clause 4.1 does not apply, and the contract date governs. 7.1 Scope
7.1.1 This section applies to claims under the Home Contents Plus and Home Contents Essentials policy wordings where the loss arises from escape of water from a fixed installation at the insured property.
7.1.2 Claims for damage caused by flood, rising groundwater or external ingress are assessed under Section 8.

7.2 Excess and limits
7.2.1 The standard voluntary excess is £250 per claim.
7.2.2 Escape of water claims are subject to a sub-limit of £5,000 unless the schedule states otherwise.

7.3 Exception: prior notification
7.3.1 Clause 7.3.2 applies only where the insured notified Halcyon of a leak, or of a suspected leak, within 72 hours of first becoming aware of it, and the notification is recorded on the claim system with a timestamp.
7.3.2 Where 7.3.1 is met, the sub-limit in 7.2.2 shall not apply and the claim shall be assessed to the full sum insured for the affected item.

7.4 Evidence
7.4.1 The handler shall obtain at least two independent moisture readings from the affected surfaces, recorded in percent (%) on the calibrated meter, taken on separate visits.

Coordinator's Office – Standard Operating Procedure extract
SOP-CO-014 v3.2 – Visit Windows, Sample Handling and Deviations
Effective 1 March 2026. Controlled copy: site file, binder section 4.

4.1 Scope
This procedure applies to all scheduled study visits for protocol RCU-LM-22 (Study Lipid Modulation, Phase II) and to all biological samples collected at those visits.

4.2 Visit windows
4.2.1 Each scheduled visit has a target day and a window expressed as days from Day 1 (randomisation).
4.2.2 Visits outside the window are recorded as protocol deviations and reported to the sponsor within 5 working days.
4.2.3 Visits may be rescheduled by the coordinator only within the window. Any change to the target day requires written approval from the principal investigator (PI).

4.3 Sample collection and processing
4.3.1 Fasting bloods must be drawn between 07:30 and 09:00. Samples drawn outside this range are labelled "non-fasting" on the requisition.
4.3.2 Serum tubes are allowed to clot for 30 minutes before centrifugation at 1,500 g for 10 minutes.
4.3.3 Samples must be placed in the −80 °C freezer within 90 minutes of collection.

4.4 Exceptions
4.4.1 Where a participant's visit falls outside the window because of a documented illness, the PI may approve a visit up to 7 days beyond the upper limit. Approval must be recorded on form RCU-F-09 before the visit takes place.
4.4.2 Samples held beyond 90 minutes at room temperature because of equipment failure may be retained if the freezer log and the courier manifest are both filed with the sample record.

Case note – CN-2026-031
Participant RCU-LM-22-107, Visit 4 (target Day 84, window Days 77–91)
Visit 4 took place on Day 96. The participant reported a chest infection on Day 80 and attended a GP appointment on Day 81, a copy of which is in the source file. 7. TEMPERATURE EXCURSIONS

7.1 Chilled product (setpoint 2°C to 8°C) is rejected at receipt if the probe reading exceeds 8.0°C at the time of unloading.

7.2 Frozen product (setpoint −18°C or colder) is held in quarantine if any logged reading is warmer than −15.0°C for more than 30 consecutive minutes.

7.3 Any excursion recorded under 7.1 or 7.2 is reported to the Quality Duty Officer within 2 working days of the event. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays observed in England.

7.4 Quarantined stock is assessed by the Quality Duty Officer and released, downgraded or destroyed under form QA-F-22 (Disposition Record).

7.5 Exception: where a carrier's own data logger shows the reading was within limits for the full transit period and the depot probe was faulty, the Quality Duty Officer may release the load under 7.2 with a countersigned calibration certificate dated no more than 90 days before the event.

Policy extract: BIL-P-14 Estimated Reads and Back-Billing
Version 3.2 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Head of Billing Operations | Review due 31 March 2027

14.1 Scope
This clause applies to domestic and small business accounts where a meter reading has not been obtained within the billing period, and where a bill has been issued on an estimate.

14.2 Estimated reads
Where no actual read has been received for 90 days or more, the billing agent must raise a Read Request (RR) through the field portal before any estimated bill is reissued. The RR must state the last actual read, its date, and the Meter Serial Number (MSN) as held on the Meter Asset Register.

14.3 Back-billing limit
A supplier may not back-bill a customer for consumption older than 12 months from the date the actual read is obtained, except where clause 14.4 applies.

14.4 Exception: customer-caused access failure
Where a customer has been given at least two written access notices and the back-billed amount relates to consumption not older than 24 months, back-billing may proceed up to the 24-month limit. The agent must record the notice references (AN-number) on the account before issuing the adjusted bill.

14.5 Customer communication
Any adjusted bill above £150.00 must be preceded by a written explanation sent no less than 10 working days before the bill date. Verbal explanations do not satisfy this clause.

21:40  CHG-88213 approved at CAB extraordinary session (ref CAB-X-0092), conditions: canary on pg-edge-06 for 30 min.

Tomasz Sørensen (L2): "Node 06 was never in the rollback list. I assumed the template had been applied everywhere it was supposed to be."
Agnieszka Bello (Support lead): "The ticket volume spiked around 23:30 and then dropped quickly after the fix. Several customers said they were charged twice. We have not verified that yet."

4. Reactive repair response
4.1 Priority 1 faults (no water, no power to a floor, lift out of service with a passenger trapped or a fire alarm fault) must be attended within 4 working hours of logging.
4.2 Priority 2 faults (single room without heating or lighting, door entry fault, toilet out of use on a floor with one other toilet) must be attended within 2 working days of logging.

4.4 Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and English bank holidays. Working hours are 08:00 to 17:30 Monday to Thursday and 08:00 to 16:00 Friday.
4.5 Where a job is logged after 15:00 on a working day, the clock starts at 08:00 on the next working day.

5. Closure and partial resolution
5.1 A fault is closed only when all of the following are met: (a) the defect is no longer present, (b) the reporting tenant confirms by reply to the ticket, and (c) the work order is signed off in the CAFM system.
5.2 A fault where two of the three conditions in 5.1 are met is recorded as "Partly resolved" and remains open for a further 5 working days.
5.3 A fault where only one of the three conditions in 5.1 is met is recorded as "Awaiting completion" and does not count toward response statistics.

6. Exceptions
6.1 Clause 4.3 does not apply to tenants in Suite 3 or Suite 4 during the fit-out period notified under lease schedule 2, where the repair window is extended to 15 working days.

4.1 Where a householder application seeks retention of works already carried out, the validating officer shall record the date works were first observed by the Council, using the Enforcement Log reference where one exists.

4.2 Evidence of works completed more than four years before the application date may be accepted in lieu of a Lawful Development Certificate, provided it is corroborated by at least two independent sources (aerial imagery, dated photographs, utility connection records, or sworn statements).

4.3 Where evidence from a single source conflicts with evidence from another source, the validating officer shall give greater weight to contemporaneous records (dated imagery and utility records) over statements made after the event.

4.4 Criteria weighting: where criteria pull in different directions, the criterion relating to the safety of occupants and neighbours takes precedence over the criterion relating to the age of works. Visual amenity is weighted equally with age of works.

3. Scoring of Roof Survey Criteria

3.1 Each completed site survey is scored against four criteria: (a) roof covering condition (scale 1–5), (b) rafter/truss integrity as recorded on the structural checklist (pass / conditional / fail), (c) shading factor (percentage of annual irradiance lost, from the shading tool), and (d) customer-reported load history (free text, verified by surveyor).

3.2 Priority of criteria. Where criteria conflict, structural integrity (3.1(b)) takes precedence over all other criteria. A "fail" result cannot be overridden by any other criterion except as set out in clause 5.3. Shading and roof covering condition are weighted equally with each other and are secondary to structural integrity.

3.3 Survey observations recorded by the surveyor on the handheld device take precedence over third-party reports supplied by the customer, unless the third-party report is an engineer's certificate issued within the preceding 24 months.

4. Installation Eligibility

4.1 A roof is eligible for standard installation where the structural checklist reads "pass" and roof covering condition is 3 or above.

4.2 A roof reading "conditional" under 3.1(b) requires a structural addendum (form SC-F7) signed by a Chartered Engineer before scheduling.

4.3 Roofs with shading factor above 22% are referred to the Design desk for string layout review before quotation. Referral does not by itself make a roof ineligible.

5. Exceptions and Reinstatement

5.1 Installations previously declined under 4.1 may be re-surveyed once the recorded defect has been remedied and evidenced.

5.2 Re-surveys must be carried out by a surveyor other than the original.

5.3 Where an engineer's certificate under 3.3 confirms that a rafter defect recorded as "fail" has been fully remediated, the Head of Surveys may approve installation provided that: (i) the certificate post-dates the original survey by at least 60 days; (ii) the rafter area concerned has had no further reported incident; and (iii) the roof covering scores 4 or above. Approval must be recorded on form SC-F9 with the reference of the certificate.

6. Records

6.1 All survey outcomes are held on the job record in the CRM under the field names listed in Annex B.

Internal Policy Extract: Container Demurrage and Detention Liability
Policy ref: OPS-DEM-04 | Revision 3 | Effective 1 March 2026 | Owner: Head of Ocean Operations

4. Demurrage: chargeable period and liability

4.1 Demurrage is chargeable by the carrier for each full or part day a laden or empty container remains in the terminal beyond the free time stated on the carrier's booking confirmation. Free time begins at 00:00 on the day after discharge is recorded at the terminal gate-out system.

4.2 The company is liable for demurrage only where the delay is attributable to the consignee, the customs broker or the company's own booking actions, as recorded under clause 4.4.

4.3 Where a carrier invoice is received, the Booking Desk shall match it against the gate-in and gate-out timestamps from the terminal portal and record the match result in field DEM-MATCH on the shipment file within two working days of receipt.

4.4 Each delay shall be assigned one cause code from the following list: CONS (consignee not ready), CUST (customs hold or inspection), BOOK (booking error or late instruction), CARR (carrier or terminal fault), WTHR (weather or port closure). Cause codes must be supported by at least one dated observation on the shipment file.

4.5 EXCEPTION: Where a carrier or terminal fault (CARR) is confirmed in writing by the terminal operator, the company is not liable for the resulting demurrage and the charge shall be referred to the carrier for credit. Written confirmation must be attached to the shipment file before the cause code is set.

4.6 EXCEPTION: For WTHR delays, liability is shared equally between the company and the consignee, unless the consignee has been notified of the closure in writing within 24 hours, in which case the consignee bears the full charge.

4.7 Verbal confirmation from terminal staff is not sufficient evidence for clause 4.5 and must be recorded only as a provisional note pending written confirmation.

---

Prepared by: R. Okonkwo, Booking Desk | Date: 27 October 2026

Container MSKU-4471926 discharged on 9 October 2026. Terminal gate-out system shows gate-out on 19 October at 14:52. Free time per carrier confirmation was 4 days from the day after discharge. Carrier invoice INV-88213 claims 6 days demurrage at £95 per day, total £570.

Brennan, 15 October, says the fault was "probably" the terminal's and that a written statement would follow. No written statement is on file as at today.

Consignee (Ashcroft Tools Ltd) emailed on 13 October stating their warehouse was not ready to receive until the 18th. This email is on file. No written WTHR notice was sent by the company to the consignee.

Section 7: Out-of-Hours Call-Outs, Water Ingress and Plant Alarms
Effective: 1 September 2026
